Status.note: The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists Plant 1122, generator 7, as operating with 37.5 MW. The City of Ames electric department page says Unit 7 is in service.

Start year.note: A Sargent and Lundy project page says the City of Ames converted its Unit 7 and Unit 8 boilers from coal to natural gas. The project started in May 2014 and was completed in July 2016. So the unit first ran on gas in 2016, not 1968. The 1968 year is when the coal unit began operating.

qa.recommendation: The City of Ames page says Unit 7 burns refuse derived fuel from municipal solid waste along with natural gas. GEM lists only natural gas. Consider adding a bioenergy fuel for waste. The page also says the city has started to phase this fuel out.

qa.recommendation: The City of Ames plans to retire Units 7 and 8 when the new Ames Energy Center opens. A city podcast episode from November 2025 describes this. Local news says the new plant, built from reciprocating engines, will open in 2029. I found no firm retirement year from the city, so I did not report one.
qa.note: Retirement is planned but no firm year was found. Both units are still operating.
